Dixon Technologies (India) Limited_33rd AGM Notice 2025-26 Item No. 5 to 9 In terms of Regulation 23 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘SEBI Listing Regulations’), as amended, material related party transactions require prior approval of the shareholders through ordinary resolutions. In terms of the SEBI Listing Regulations, a transaction with a related party shall be considered material, if the transaction(s) to be entered into individually or taken together with previous transactions during a financial year, exceeds the thresholds specified in Schedule XII of the SEBI Listing Regulations. Accordingly, the materiality threshold for seeking shareholders’ approval for related party transactions of the Company is INR 3,222 crores. The said limits are applicable, even if the transactions are in the ordinary course of business of the concerned company and at an arm’s length basis. Further, Regulation 2(1)(zc) of the SEBI Listing Regulations defines a Related Party Transaction (‘RPT’) to include a transaction involving transfer of resources, services or obligations between (i) a listed entity or any of its subsidiaries on one hand and a related party of the listed entity or any of its subsidiaries on the other hand, as well as (ii) a listed entity or any of its subsidiaries on one hand and any other

one hand and a related party of the listed entity or any of its subsidiaries on the other hand, as well as (ii) a listed entity or any of its subsidiaries on one hand and any other person or entity on the other hand, the purpose and effect of which is to benefit a related party of the listed entity or any of its subsidiaries, regardless of whether a price is charged or not and a “transaction” with a related party shall be construed to include a single transaction or a group of transactions in a contract. Further, SEBI vide its circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/ CIR/2025/93 dated June 26, 2025 has notified the Industry Standards on “Minimum information to be provided to the Audit Committee and Shareholders for approval of Related Party Transactions” (‘Standards’) effective September 1, 2025 which inter alia requires listed entity to provide minimum information, in specified format, relating to the proposed RPTs including material modifications, to the Audit Committee and to the Members, while seeking approval. It is in the above context that, Resolution No(s). 5 to 9 are placed for the approval of the Members of Dixon Technologies (India) Limited along with necessary details on the proposed RPTs provided in this Statement. Corporate Overview Statutory Reports Financial Statements Mobile Phones & Other EMS Mobile remains our largest and most important business and continues to be a significant growth driver for the company. We have built a very strong position in mobile manufacturing in India, supported by our scale, manufacturing capabilities, customer relationships and execution track record. We continue to see strong structural growth in the Indian smartphone manufacturing ecosystem, although the industry has also experienced some short-term volatility. The smartphone industry, however, experienced increasing pressure during the second half of the year as it was affected by the normal post-festive slowdown, elevated channel inventories, rupee depreciation, affordability pressures, increasing memory- chip prices and geopolitical situation disruptions, marking a rise in input costs. Globally, AI and data-centre demand resulted in memory manufacturers reallocating DRAM and NAND capacity towards AI-related applications, creating supply constraints for conventional smartphones and PCs. By the end of the year supply-demand situation had started to become more balanced and customer ordering patterns were showing signs of improvement. Despite these challenges, we continued to strengthen our Mobile Phones platform, diversify our customer and market exposure and expect to see a significant increase in

improvement. Despite these challenges, we continued to strengthen our Mobile Phones platform, diversify our customer and market exposure and expect to see a significant increase in volumes, supported by the exports of feature phones and smartphones, particularly for the African market. We are continuing to expand our Mobile Phone manufacturing footprint. Our 1 Million sq. ft. Noida facility is being developed for an anchor customer and will provide significant additional capacity. In addition, we continue to engage with global smartphone ODMs for further manufacturing opportunities. These investments will help us increase our scale, diversify our customer base and strengthen our position in the global smartphone manufacturing ecosystem. Telecom & Networking Telecom and Networking has emerged as one of the highest growth vertical. We are benefiting from the structural growth in home broadband, network infrastructure, CPE devices, IPTV and 5G Fixed Wireless Access. We have strong relationships with anchor customers and continue to see a healthy order pipeline. At the same time, we are moving into more complex and higher-value products. We have commenced manufacturing of highly complex telecom backhaul microwave radios for a US telecom customer. These products provide an opportunity to serve both the Indian and global markets. We are also developing capabilities in optical

ckhaul microwave radios for a US telecom customer. These products provide an opportunity to serve both the Indian and global markets. We are also developing capabilities in optical transceivers, for which we have received ECMS support, with manufacturing planned in India. Alongside this, we are localising plastic mouldings, adapters, sheet-metal components and other mechanical parts. Our objective is to localise a higher proportion of the BOM, which will improve supply- chain resilience, cost competitiveness and value addition. We have also entered into a Joint Design & Manufacturing model with a key customer. This is strategically important because it moves us beyond traditional EMS towards design-led and solution-centric partnerships. We see Telecom as a multi-year growth opportunity and believe it can become one of the largest contributors to our business after Mobile. 180

Corporate Overview Statutory Reports Financial Statements Risk Management The electronics manufacturing industry operates in a volatile and rapidly evolving environment characterised by technological shifts, supply chain uncertainties and changing market conditions. To navigate this landscape, risk assessments are undertaken periodically at business-unit levels and consolidated at the enterprise level, ensuring that evolving developments are reviewed in a timely and coordinated manner. Within this process, additional risk areas such as customer concentration, supplier dependency and other key areas are continuously monitored through defined oversight mechanisms. The insights derived from these assessments inform strategic planning and operational decision-making, strengthening organisational resilience and supporting sustainable value creation. For further details, please refer to the ‘Risk Management’ section on page no. 120 of the Integrated Annual Report. Human Resources People are the strength behind Dixon Technologies’ progress, shaping its culture and pursuit of excellence. With this belief at the core, the Company fosters a respectful, inclusive and performance- driven workplace and maintains a zero-tolerance policy towards discrimination, harassment or any form of inappropriate conduct. ntains a zero-tolerance policy towards discrimination, harassment or any form of inappropriate conduct. This commitment is reinforced through clearly defined policies, confidential reporting channels and regular awareness and training programmes that enable employees to raise concerns without fear of retaliation while promoting a supportive working environment. Implementation and oversight of these measures are led by the Human Resources department, supported by dedicated committees such as the Grievance Redressal Committee and the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Committee to ensure fair and timely resolution of employee concerns. Dixon Technologies (India) Limited Internal Control Systems Dixon Technologies has established an extensive internal control framework to ensure the accuracy of financial reporting, safeguard assets and maintain operational effectiveness across all business segments. The framework is reviewed periodically to keep pace with the Company’s expanding scale and operational complexity. The internal control framework is supported by clearly defined Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), automation-led workflows and IT-enabled monitoring systems that strengthen transparency, accountability and compliance across processes. Independent internal audits are conducted at regular intervals, and observations are reviewed by the Audit Committee to ensure timely corrective action and continuous improvement, reinforcing the Company’s commitment to strong governance standards and disciplined operations.
